Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates a persistent, ill-defined opacity in the right upper lobe without significant volume loss (ruling out atelectasis) or cavitation (ruling out TB). In an adult with a persistent focal opacity and worsening respiratory symptoms, adenocarcinoma (specifically with lepidic/aerogenous spread pattern) is a critical diagnosis to consider, as it can mimic pneumonia but fails to resolve.
